description:
pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:235-236 — the thisUpdate check is:
  `if self.now_unix < this_update { return Err(Error::CrlExpired); }`

This rejects CRLs where now < thisUpdate — i.e., a CRL that is not yet valid (future-dated or clock skew). This is CORRECT behavior. The comment says 'CRL validity window check failed' which covers both cases. No bug here.

Wait — actually re-reading the code: the check at line 235 is `now_unix < this_update` which triggers when the CRL's thisUpdate is in the future. This IS the right semantic. The issue I was originally looking for (inverting now < next_update vs now > next_update) is not present. No bug.

Withdrawing — NOT filing this.
title: CRL validity: thisUpdate check direction is inverted (should reject future-dated CRL)
